 JUDGMENT

This claim petition is filed by the petitioners claiming compensation of .1,00,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for death of Sri.K.Vijaya Kumar, S/o.Late.Kishan Das in a road traffic accident.

2. The petition averments in brief is that on 28.10.2019 deceased boarded the KSRTC Bus bearing Regn.No.KA-09-F-4754 in Mysuru to reach Virajpet and bus stopped in Virajpet bus stop, while deceased was de- boarding the bus the driver of bus suddenly moved the bus without getting any signal from conductor.

Due to which, deceased slipped from bus and fallen on ground and sustained grievous injuries and thereafter deceased was taken to nearby Athreya Hospital and then shifted to Bhagwan Mahaveer Jain Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein took treatment as an inpatient and discharged and later on he succumbed to the injuries.
Prior to the accident, deceased was hale and healthy and was business man and Coffee Planter and earning a sum of Rs.10,00,000/- per annum.
Due to untimely death of deceased, petitioners life has become dark, miserable and depressed and put to great financial hardship.
The accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of said KSRTC Bus by its driver.
The respondents being Managing Director and driver of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to petitioners.
3. On service of notice, respondent No.1 appeared before the tribunal through his counsel and filed his written statement.
The respondent No.2 did not appear before the tribunal hence, he has been placed as exparte.
4. In his written statement, the respondent No.1 has denied the contents of claim petition specifically and categorically.
He has also denied age, occupation and income of deceased.
He has also denied the place, time and manner of accident.
The petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed.
Further this respondent denied that there was no rashness or negligence on the part of driver of KSRTC Bus.

Further contended that on the date and time of alleged accident, the bus in question was on its schedule trip from Mysuru to Virajpet and bus was being driven by its driver and while so proceeding and reached its destination at Virajpet bus stand, the driver stopped the bus in bus stand at plat form and got down from the bus and passengers were alighting from bus, and when the things stood thus, the deceased who had leg injury lost the balance and fell down from the bus.

As such, for the alleged accident the deceased himself was wholly and solely responsible but the driver of bus in question was no way responsible Smt.V.Padma vs The Managing Director on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90352760/

sentences.text: as the bus was stopped long back.
Further this respondent denied the relationship of deceased and petitioners.
The amount claimed by the petitioners is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prayed for dismissal of petition.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following:
ISSUES 1.

Whether petitioners prove that the husband of petitioner No.1 and father of petitioner No.2 & 3 namely K.Vijaya Kumar succumbed to the injuries sustained in the acciden that took place on 28.10.2019 at about 07.15 to 7.60 p.m., KSRTC Bus Stand, Virajpete Town, Kodagu District, while he was alighting from the KSRTC Bus,
due to the rash and negligent driving of the KSRTC Bus bearing Registration No.KA-09-F-4754 by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?

6. The petitioners in support of their case, the petitioner No.1/wife of deceased examined as PW.1,
Sri.C.M.Basappa examined as PW.2 and Dr.N.Prakash examined as PW.3 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.32 and closed their side of evidence.
On the other hand, the driver of KSRTC Bus examined as RW.1 and no documents have been marked on his behalf and closed his side of evidence.
7. I have heard arguments on both side and perused materials available on records.

8. My answer to the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative.

Issue No.1:- In this case the petitioners contend that on 28.10.2019 at about 19:15 to 19:60 hrs,
Near KSRTC Bus Stand, Virajpet Town, Kodagu District, the deceased Sri.K.Vijaya Kumar had met with an accident due to rash and negligent driving of KSRTC Bus bearing Regn.No.KA-09-F- 4754 by its driver and he succumbed to the injuries.

3 10.
The petitioner No.1/wife of deceased examined as PW.1 and produced Ex.P.1 and 2 FIR and first information.
On perusal of Ex.P.2, deceased petitioner by Sri.Vijaya Kumar has given first information to police on 31.10.2019 and accident occurred on 28.10.2019.
On the basis of Ex.P.2 police registered a case as per Ex.P.1.
He has stated in his complaint that due to rash and negligent driving of KSRTC Bus by its driver the accident occurred.
After registering case Police went near place of accident and drew up spot mahazar as per Ex.P.3 by narrating the place of accident.
After investigation police filed charge sheet as per Ex.P.4 against driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.279 & 304-(A) of IPC.
On the other hand, the driver of KSRTC examined as RW.1 and no documents have been marked on his behalf.

RW.1 in his chief examination, he has deposed that the deceased who had leg injury lost balance and fell down from the bus, as such deceased himself was wholly and solely responsible and there was no negligence of him as the bus was stopped long back.
On perusal of chief examination of RW.1, the deceased sustained injuries while alighting from the bus.
There is no evidence before the tribunal to show that the deceased himself fell down from the bus while he was alighting.
The respondent KSRTC also not examined eye witness before the tribunal to establish their contention.
As per police documents placed by the petitioner when deceased was alighting from bus the driver of KSRTC Bus moved his bus, as a result he fell down and sustained injuries.
The respondent has not rebutted the police documents.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P.5, this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of KSRTC Bus bearing Regn.No.KA-09-F-4754 by its driver and deceased sustained injuries.
11. The petitioners contended that due to injuries sustained by deceased in accident, he succumbed to injuries.
The petitioners have produced Ex.P.14 - Discharge Summary.

As per Ex.P.14, the deceased Sri.K.Vijaya Kumar admitted to Bhagwan Mahaveer Jain Hospital on 29.10.2019, wherein the doctor diagnosed that Type IV intertrochantric fracture with subtrochantric extension left femur.
Further in same document, it is mentioned in past history that known case of Hypertension & Diabetes on treatment and history of surgery to left forearm 2 years back.

Further the petitioner also produced Ex.P.15 - Discharge Summary, wherein he admitted on 03.12.2019 and discharged on 08.01.2020, wherein the doctor diagnosed that sepsis with septic shock, acute kidney injury, hpoxic ischemic encephalopathy, old pulmonary embolism, herpes simplex erythema multiforme, diabetes and hypertension.

Further in same document, the past history was known case of Hypertension on Tab, Almong 5mg 1-0-1, Tab.Prolomet XL 50 mg 1-0-1, diabetes mellitus since 6 years, Ischemic Heart disease on Nov 2019, Pulmonary Thromboembolism, History of HIE S/P Cardiac Arrest acute kidney injury S/P 3 cycles of haemodialysis, history of ORIF on 29.10.2019.

Further petitioners produced Ex.P.26 - Case sheet of Bhagwan Mahaveer Jain Hospital, wherein in discharge summary,
it is mentioned that complaints of sudden onset breathing difficulty since today afternoon.

Further the petitioner produced Ex.P.23 - Medical Certificate of Cause of death issued by Bhagwan Mahaveer Jain Hospital, wherein the said document was issued on 11.01.2020 and wherein mentioned that brought dead.

Thereafter the dead body was shifted to Bowring & Lady Curzon Medical College & Research Institute, Bengaluru, and conducted postmortem on 11.01.2020 and opinion for cause of death kept pending for Histopathology report.

sentences.text: Further deposed that patient alleged history of fall while getting out of bus as the bus moved forward accidentally.
Due to this he had fall and complained of pain in left hip.

Further in his chief examination, he has deposed that he was clinically diagnosed as left hip fracture and there was surgery of left hip, the surgery was done on 31.10.2019 and underwent proximal femur nailing.
Then he was shifted to ward from recovery room.
So, as per Discharge Summary produced by petitioner diagnosed that Type IV intertrochantric fracture with subtrochantric extension left femur.
PW.3 in his cross examination, he has deposed that the patient improved systematically and discharged.
Further in his cross examination deposed that there was a cardiac arrest and they have given treatment for that and thereafter died due to multiple organ failure.
On perusal of chief examination of PW.3, the doctor has only deposed that course of treatment given in the hospital, but PW.3 not deposed definite cause of death.
Further on perusal of chief examination and cross examination of PW.3, there is no evidence due to injuries sustained by deceased, he died.
As per Ex.P.14, the doctor diagnosed the fracture with subtrochantric extension left femur and treatment was given.

Further in same document at Para.4 of course in the hospital, it is mentioned as follows:
"patient is a known case of diabetes & hypertension.
Patient underwent left femur ORIF with PFN on 31.10.2019.
POT op period patient developed 1 episode of seizure followed by sudden cardiac arrest.
Patient was resuscitated & shifted to ICU for further management.
Subsequent investigation showed - MRI brain - Hypoxic ischaemic encephalopathy.
CTPA - saddle embolus involving the bifurcation of main pulmonary trunk.

Cardiologist, pulmonologist, urologist opinions were taken &
patient was managed as advised.
ENT opinion taken for Tracheostomy which was done on 07.11.2019.
On 09.11.2019 patient was diagnosed with acute coronary syndrome.
In view of fever spikes blood, suction tip, CVP cultures were done.
Multiple organisms were isolated from cultures (Acinetobacter baumannii - moderate growth).
Patient was started on appropriate antibiotics (Inj. Polymyxin).
Renal functions were monitored.
In view of renal impairment, nephrologist opinion was taken & patient underwent 3 cycls of haemodialysis.
Patient developed malaena.
LFT were deranged.
Patient also developed coagulopathy, with fall in haemoglobin.
Patient was transfused 8 FFP & 2 PRBC for stablization.
Gasrtroenterologist opinion was taken.
Upper GI endoscopy was done which showed panerosive gastritis.
Patient was haemodynamically stable, off ventilatory support, GCS: E4 M1 VT.
Patient shifted to ward.

Reference was given to Nephrologist, ENT Surgeon, Neuro Rehabilitation, Medical Gastroentrologist for discharge on advice, advice obtained and followed."
12.
On perusal of inpatient record produced by petitioner and discharge summary, the deceased was known case of Hypertension & Diabetes.
There was sudden cardiac arrest when he was in hospital.
After treatment, he was discharged and when he was in his home, he had developed breathing problem and then shifted to hospital as per Ex.P.26 document.
The doctor issued Death Certificate by stating that brought dead.

The petitioner produced Ex.P.24 document issued by Bowring & Lady Curzon Hospital, wherein mentioned as follows:

So, the doctor has opined that death is due to coronary artery disease.
The petitioners except examining the Orthopaedic Surgeon, they have not examined the doctor who conducted the PM Report and doctor who has issued Ex.P.24 document.

On perusal of documents placed by petitioner,
it shows that the deceased died due to cardiac arrest, there is no evidence before the tribunal to show that there was cardiac arrest due to injuries sustained by deceased in road traffic accident.
On perusal of hospital documents placed by petitioner, I am of the opinion that, there is no nexus between the accidental injuries and death.
Hence, I answered Issue No.1 Partly in the Affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:
This tribunal already held that the deceased sustained injuries while alighting from the bus, but death is not due to accidental injuries, as such the petitioners are entitled for medical expenses.

14. The learned counsel for respondent relied upon citations reported in:
(i) ILR 1990 KAR 4300 in between Kannamma Vs. Deputy General Manager,
wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka Full Bench at Para No.12 held as follows:
"12.

In the result, the Full Bench answers the question referred for its decision by the Division Bench thus:
(i) A claim petition presented under Section 110A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939, by the person sustaining bodily injuries in a motor accident, claiming compensation for personal injuries as also for compensation towards expenses, loss of income, etc.,
(loss of estate) cannot, on such person's death occurring not as a result or consequence of bodily injuries sustained from a motor accident, be prosecuted by his/her legal representatives; but (ii) A claim petition presented Under section 110A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939, by the person sustaining bodily injuries in a motor accident, claiming compensation for personal injuries as also for compensation towards expenses, loss of income, etc.,

(loss of estate) can, on such person's death occurring as a result or consequence of bodily injuries sustained in the motor accident, be prosecuted by his/her legal representatives only in so far as the claim for compensation in that claim petition relates to loss to estate of the deceased person due to bodily injuries sustained in the motor accident."

(ii) ILR 2002 KAR 1864 in between Uttam Kumar Vs. Madhav and another, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka Full Bench held that:
"Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (Central Act No.59 of 1988)

15. This court rely upon the Judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court decided on 16.08.2021 in Civil Appeal No.4800 of 2021 between The Oriental Insurance Company Limited Vs. Kahlon @ Jasmail Singh Kahlon (deceased) through his Legal Representative Narinder Kahlon Gosakan and Another,
wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court at Para No.18 & 20 held as follows:

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Company Limited Vs. Kahlon @ Jasmail Singh Kahlon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "18. The Tribunal, on technicalities rejected his claim for salary, medical expenses and percentage of disability and granted a measly compensation of Rupees one lakh only by a cryptic order.

We are, therefore, of the opinion that while the claim for personal injuries may not have survived after the death of the injured unrelated to the accident or injuries, during the pendency of the appeal, but the claims for loss of estate caused was available to and could be pursued by the legal representatives of the deceased in the appeal."
20.

We see no reason to deviate from the consistent judicial view taken by more than one High Court that loss of estate would include expenditure on medicines, treatment, diet, attendant,
doctor's fee, etc. including income and future prospects which would have caused reasonable accretion to the estate but for the sudden expenditure which had to be met from and depleted the estate of the injured, subsequently deceased."

7
With due respect to the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India and Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, the ratio laid down in the above judgments are applicable to the case on hand.
Hence, the petitioners are entitled for medical expenses.
16. The petitioners have claimed compensation towards medical expenses.
The petitioners have produced Ex.P.19 - 100 Medical bills for Rs.19,23,525/-.

In Ex.P.19 - Bill No.18 & 19, the amount paid by Apollo Munich and bill No.2, 4, 5, 7, 10 to 13, 15, 17, 29, 34, 44, 51, 57, 63, 71 & 87 are the Deposit Receipts, hence this tribunal has not considered these bills.
The respondents not rebutted the other medical bills by placing cogent evidence.
So, Tribunal is of the view that compensation of .3,22,263/- is just and reasonable towards medical expenses.
The petitioners have spent money in hospital in addition to medical expenses.

Hence, petitioners are entitled for Global compensation of Rs.4,00,000/-.
17.

In MFA.No.100090 of 2014 C/w.
MFA.No.25107 of 2013 between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs. Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka at Page No.7 at Para No.15 held as follows:
"However, the provisions of Section 149(1) of the Act to the extent they speak of interest payable on the compensation amount is in the nature of an exception to the general law enacted in 169 of the M.V.Act and therefore, the provisions of Section 34 of CPC to that extent become invocable on the general principles of construction of statutes namely the special law overrides the general law.

entities.text: Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs. Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, in the absence of any other law relating to interest on Judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Section 34 of CPC, 1908.

Thus, in the given circumstances of this case,
interest at the rate of more than 6% could not have been awarded."

In view of ratio and dictum laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the above judgment, the petitioners are entitled for interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
18. This tribunal already held that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent KSRTC Bus by its driver.
Except oral contention in the objection, the respondent has not placed any material before this tribunal to prove his contention.
Even the police authorities have not filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.181 of M.V.Act.
So, the respondent No.1 and 2 being the owner and driver of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence, Issue No.2 answered Partly in the Affirmative.

19. Issue No.3: For the forgoing reasons and in view of above discussion, Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act is allowed with cost.

The petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for compensation of .4,00,000/- (Rupees Four Lakhs only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of realization.
Respondent No.1 & 2 are joint and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Respondent No.1 being the owner is liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.
Out of the total compensation amount, the petitioners No.1 being the wife of deceased is entitled for 50% and Petitioner No.2 & 3 being the children of deceased are entitled for 25% each.

In total amount apportioned to the share of petitioners No.1 to 3, 60% of the amount shall be released in favour of petitioner No.1 to 3 and remaining 40% of the amount shall be deposited in their names in any Nationalized bank or Schedule Bank near to their place for a period of 3 years without encumbrance.
They are entitled for interest that accrues on F.D periodically.

After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA No.2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated 19.8.2019.

The petitioners hereby directed to produce particulars of Bank Account of petitioners, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contained compulsorily photographs of petitioners, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.
Further petitioners shall produce PAN Card/Adhar Card.
In case of deposit of awarded amount with interest thereon by respondent, the petitioners are entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.
Bank shall not advance loan on such FD, and shall not cause premature release of FD without permission from the Tribunal.

Bank shall release amount along with interest thereon in favour of petitioners on proper verification and identification or credit said amount to their account after expiry of three years period of deposit,
without waiting for further order of court.
The advocate fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Office to draw Award accordingly.

The respondents being Managing Director and driver of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to petitioners.
3. On service of notice, respondent No.1 appeared before the tribunal through his counsel and filed his written statement.
The respondent No.2 did not appear before the tribunal hence, he has been placed as exparte.
He has also denied age, occupation and income of deceased.
The petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed.
Further this respondent denied that there was no rashness or negligence on the part of driver of KSRTC Bus.
As such, for the alleged accident the deceased himself was wholly and solely responsible but the driver of bus in question was no way responsible Smt.V.Padma vs The Managing Director on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90352760/
2
As per police documents placed by the petitioner when deceased was alighting from bus the driver of KSRTC Bus moved his bus, as a result he fell down and sustained injuries.
On perusal of documents placed by petitioner,
it shows that the deceased died due to cardiac arrest, there is no evidence before the tribunal to show that there was cardiac arrest due to injuries sustained by deceased in road traffic accident.

due to the rash and negligent driving of the KSRTC Bus bearing Registration No.KA-09-F-4754 by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?
Issue No.1:- In this case the petitioners contend that on 28.10.2019 at about 19:15 to 19:60 hrs,
Near KSRTC Bus Stand, Virajpet Town, Kodagu District, the deceased Sri.K.Vijaya Kumar had met with an accident due to rash and negligent driving of KSRTC Bus bearing Regn.No.KA-09-F- 4754 by its driver and he succumbed to the injuries.

In the result, the Full Bench answers the question referred for its decision by the Division Bench thus:
(i) A claim petition presented under Section 110A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939, by the person sustaining bodily injuries in a motor accident, claiming compensation for personal injuries as also for compensation towards expenses, loss of income, etc.,
(loss of estate) cannot, on such person's death occurring not as a result or consequence of bodily injuries sustained from a motor accident, be prosecuted by his/her legal representatives; but (ii) A claim petition presented Under section 110A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939, by the person sustaining bodily injuries in a motor accident, claiming compensation for personal injuries as also for compensation towards expenses, loss of income, etc.,

"Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (Central Act No.59 of 1988)

Deputy General Manager ILR 1990 Karnataka 4300 may require reconsideration in view of the Amended Provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act and law laid down by the Supreme Court in some later decisions, referred the question to the Full Bench."
(iii) ILR 2002 KAR 660 in between Baburao Salaba Manabutakar, deceased by his Lrs. Vs.
Doreswamy and others, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held that:
"Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (Central Act No.59 of 1988)
- Sections 166 and 168 - Person injured in road traffic accident dying during the pendency of his claim petition before claims Tribunal, on account of reasons other than the injuries sustained in the accident - Rights of the legal representatives to continue the proceedings - In view of the law laid down by the Division Bench of the Karnataka High Court in Muniyappa Vs. H.L.Narasimhaiah 1984(1) Karnataka Law Journal 41 and Full Bench decision in Kannamma Vs. Deputy General Manager ILR 1990 Karnataka 4300, Legal representatives cannot prosecute the claim petition presented by the injured and as such they cannot even recover Medical Expenses incurred for the treatment of injuries - Suggestion made by the Division Bench of the Karnataka High Court in Muniyappa's case to the effect."
Hence, the petitioners are entitled for medical expenses.
16. The petitioners have claimed compensation towards medical expenses.
The respondents not rebutted the other medical bills by placing cogent evidence.
So, Tribunal is of the view that compensation of .3,22,263/- is just and reasonable towards medical expenses.
The petitioners have spent money in hospital in addition to medical expenses.
Hence, petitioners are entitled for Global compensation of Rs.4,00,000/-.
17.
18. This tribunal already held that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent KSRTC Bus by its driver.
Even the police authorities have not filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.181 of M.V.Act.
So, the respondent No.1 and 2 being the owner and driver of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
opennyai_summary.decision:
19. Issue No.3: For the forgoing reasons and in view of above discussion, Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act is allowed with cost.
The petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for compensation of .4,00,000/- (Rupees Four Lakhs only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of realization.
Respondent No.1 & 2 are joint and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Respondent No.1 being the owner is liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.
Out of the total compensation amount, the petitioners No.1 being the wife of deceased is entitled for 50% and Petitioner No.2 & 3 being the children of deceased are entitled for 25% each.
In total amount apportioned to the share of petitioners No.1 to 3, 60% of the amount shall be released in favour of petitioner No.1 to 3 and remaining 40% of the amount shall be deposited in their names in any Nationalized bank or Schedule Bank near to their place for a period of 3 years without encumbrance.
They are entitled for interest that accrues on F.D periodically.
After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA No.2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated 19.8.2019.
The petitioners hereby directed to produce particulars of Bank Account of petitioners, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contained compulsorily photographs of petitioners, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.
Further petitioners shall produce PAN Card/Adhar Card.
In case of deposit of awarded amount with interest thereon by respondent, the petitioners are entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.
Bank shall not advance loan on such FD, and shall not cause premature release of FD without permission from the Tribunal.
Bank shall release amount along with interest thereon in favour of petitioners on proper verification and identification or credit said amount to their account after expiry of three years period of deposit,
without waiting for further order of court.
The advocate fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Office to draw Award accordingly.
